summary.oneLiner: Goel Construction Company Limited (GCC) is a Jaipur-based specialised industrial construction company that builds the civil infrastructure for India's heavy industries — cement plants, thermal power plants and dairy facilities — with an order book of ₹1,291 Crores.

Its customers are leading Indian industrial groups including UltraTech, Adani Power, JSW and JK Lakshmi Cement, served across 13 states with a fleet of owned construction equipment and an in-house execution workforce. currentContext.strengths: Established and preferred contractor for cement plant construction with a Pan-India presence, built on a strong track record and deep sector expertise with leading industrial clients|Asset-backed execution model: a fleet of 270+ owned construction equipment — mobile tower cranes, concrete pumps, batching plants, excavators — enabling faster mobilisation and reducing third-party dependency|Specialised engineering capability in complex cement plant structures including heavy foundations, RCC silos and high-rise structures up to ~150 metres, which transfers into power, steel and other industrial infrastructure work|Long-standing relationships with marquee industrial clients (UltraTech, Adani Power, JSW, JK Lakshmi Cement) that have resulted in repeat orders and sustained business growth|Skilled workforce of 1,400+ professionals and skilled employees, supplemented by a project workforce of 8,000+ personnel mobilised through an established network of site contractors|Capital-efficient operating model with limited working capital needs despite large projects — customer mobilisation advances, regular monthly billing and disciplined receivables management; Cash Flow from Operations equivalent to 94% of Operating Profit in FY26 and Core ROCE of 40%|Maiden CRISIL A-/Stable rating and negligible debt, which enhances project pre-qualification, financing flexibility and credibility in securing large-scale industrial projects|Track record of multiple client awards for safety, quality and execution excellence from UltraTech Cement (Kukurdih, Dhule, Hirmi) and Adani Power (Godda, Jharkhand)
currentContext.strategies: TODAY — Strengthen the core: execute the record ₹1,291 Crore order book on time and efficiently across 17 ongoing projects in 13 states, reinforcing customer confidence and execution credentials.|Scale with financial discipline — use the strong balance sheet, low debt and CRISIL A-/Stable rating to pre-qualify for and pursue larger projects, strengthen working capital flexibility and fund strategic investments in integrated capabilities.|TOMORROW — Integrated project solutions: move beyond pure civil construction by adding structural and mechanical works, positioning GCC as a one-stop industrial construction partner and lifting typical order size from ₹100-150 Crores to ₹250-400 Crores.|Sector diversification: expand beyond cement and power into steel plants, logistics parks and other process industries to broaden the addressable market and cut single-sector dependence (cement's order-book share has already fallen from 96% to 76%).|Pan-India geographic expansion: from the current 13 states into high-growth industrial regions including Bihar and Odisha, while following existing customers into new geographies.|Increase wallet share in power plants, leveraging the established BoP track record with the Adani Group as thermal capacity additions accelerate; power is already 21% of the order book.|Deepen the role across the industrial project value chain so clients can be served through a single execution partner, reducing coordination complexity and enhancing accountability.|Keep execution — quality, safety and timely delivery — as the foundation of scaling, through better planning, stronger site systems and disciplined reviews.|People and safety: strengthen the workforce through talent acquisition, continuous training and employee development, backed by a zero-harm, safety-first culture.
currentContext.expansion: GCC is a construction services business, so its 'expansion' is footprint, equipment fleet and order-book scale rather than manufacturing capacity. Physically, the Company expands through its owned equipment base — a fleet of 270+ owned construction machines including mobile tower cranes, concrete pumps, batching plants and excavators — which it says enables faster project mobilisation and reduces third-party dependency; one of the two stated objects of the September 2025 BSE SME IPO was capital expenditure towards the purchase of additional equipment and fleets (Rs 4,174.38 lakhs earmarked in the offer document, Rs 2,772.04 lakhs utilised and Rs 1,402.34 lakhs still unutilised as on 31 March 2026), with the second object, repayment/prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings (Rs 2,305.25 lakhs), fully utilised. Geographically, the Company operates across 13 states with 17 ongoing projects and over 100 completed projects, and intends to expand into high-growth industrial regions including Bihar and Odisha and other emerging industrial states. Capability-wise, GCC is extending beyond civil construction into structural and mechanical works to offer integrated, one-stop execution, and expects this to lift its typical order size from Rs 100-150 Crores to Rs 250-400 Crores over time; average project size has already grown from roughly Rs 10-20 crore in the early years to Rs 200-300 crore today. Sector expansion is into steel plants, logistics parks and other process industries alongside deeper penetration of power, where the flagship 2x800 MW Balance of Plant works for the Adani Group in Madhya Pradesh (Rs 172 Crores) was followed during FY26 by a further Rs 260 Crores Adani order; ongoing cement work spans large-scale greenfield and brownfield plants in Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and dairy work includes a completed 800 TPD Cattle Feed Plant in Gujarat and ongoing dairy infrastructure in Punjab. No commissioning or ramp-up timelines for owned assets are disclosed, as the Company builds facilities for customers rather than operating plants of its own.
currentContext.mdna: India's infrastructure-led development strategy: the Union Budget FY27 allocated a record ₹12.2 lakh crore to capital expenditure (up from ₹11.2 lakh crore in FY26), with PM Gati Shakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, National Logistics Policy and Smart Cities Mission sustaining demand for engineering and construction services.|India's construction industry contributes nearly 9% of GVA, employs 70+ million, and is expected to grow at approximately 8.1%; management expects sustained growth from infrastructure investment, rapid urbanisation and industrial development.|Industrial construction is the fastest-growing segment of the construction ecosystem, driven by rising capital expenditure across cement, steel, power, chemicals, food processing, warehousing and logistics, plus 12 industrial corridors under development, PLI coverage of 14 strategic sectors and a 25% manufacturing-to-GDP target.|Cement sector: installed capacity of ~690 MTPA against FY26 production of ~485 MT, with 6-7% demand growth expected over the medium term — continued capacity expansion and modernisation is expected to generate significant opportunities for specialised civil construction contractors.|Steel sector: National Steel Policy target of 300 MT capacity by 2030-31 against ~165 MT crude steel production; greenfield and brownfield steel plants, beneficiation and pellet plants are expected to create long-term civil construction opportunities.|Renewable power: ~250 GW installed renewable capacity against a 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030; solar parks, wind farms, substations, battery storage and green hydrogen facilities are expected to create long-term demand for civil, structural and balance-of-plant work.|Dairy sector: India is the largest milk producer with ~25% of global production and an expected industry CAGR of 8-9%; modernisation of processing infrastructure and cattle feed plants sustains capital investment.|Chairman's view that the next phase of industrialisation is driving robust demand for factories, manufacturing facilities, logistics hubs, warehouses and renewable energy assets, with India's construction sector expected to become the world's second largest by 2030 and construction GVA projected to reach ₹20.7 trillion by FY30.|Margin lever — operating leverage: FY26 EBITDA margin improvement was driven by higher project execution enabling more efficient absorption of fixed overheads, supported by disciplined project management and improved execution efficiencies.|Margin lever — capital structure: lower finance costs following repayment of borrowings through IPO proceeds contributed to the stronger bottom line; the Company continues to run negligible debt.|Cash-flow driver: an advance-based billing model with customer mobilisation advances, regular monthly billing and disciplined receivables management keeps working capital light, with CFO equivalent to 94% of operating profit in FY26.|Headwind flagged: prolonged and heavier monsoon conditions disrupted execution timelines across project sites in H1 FY26, with the shortfall recovered through stronger execution momentum in H2.|Companies with proven execution capabilities, technical expertise and long-standing customer relationships are described as best positioned to benefit from the evolving industrial landscape.|Closing order book of ₹1,291.23 Crores as at 31 March 2026 versus ₹438.49 Crores a year earlier — a nearly three-fold (2.94x) increase and the Company's highest ever.|Order inflows of over ₹1,500 Crores secured during FY26, described by the Chairman as evidence of continued client trust.|Order book to revenue of 1.96x in FY26 (0.74x in FY25, 1.42x in FY24) — approximately 2x FY26 revenue, giving strong revenue visibility over the next 18 months.|17 ongoing projects across 13 states as on March 31, 2026.|Segment mix of the order book: cement ₹982.11 Crores (76.06%), power ₹265.76 Crores (20.58%), dairy ₹43.35 Crores (3.36%); cement's share has fallen from 96% to 76% as the Company diversifies.|During FY26 the Company secured a further ₹260 Crores order from the Adani Group in the power segment, adding to the flagship 2×800 MW BoP works project in Madhya Pradesh (₹172 Crores).|Average project size has grown from approximately ₹10-20 crore in the early years to ₹200-300 crore today.

risks.note: Delays arising from design changes, site conditions, labour shortages, material availability or customer approvals may impact project schedules, costs and profitability. This is not theoretical for GCC: the Chairman reports that FY26 opened with prolonged and heavier monsoon conditions disrupting execution timelines across project sites in the first half, with the year only rescued by stronger execution momentum in H2.

A significant portion of revenue is generated from a limited number of customers and industries; any slowdown in customer capex or loss of key clients could affect business performance. The order book is anchored on a handful of large industrial groups — UltraTech, Adani Power, JSW and JK Lakshmi Cement — with a single Adani Group power project (2x800 MW BoP in Madhya Pradesh) and a further Rs 260 Crores Adani order forming a large part of the power segment.

Cement plant construction remains 76.06% of the order book and 83.93% of FY26 revenue even after the Company's stated diversification (cement's order-book share has fallen from 96% to 76%). GCC's revenue therefore tracks the cement industry's capacity-addition cycle, and the diversification into power, steel, logistics parks and process industries is still at an early stage.

Growth depends on the ability to continuously secure new orders in a competitive bidding environment; reduced order inflows would impact future revenue visibility. The FY26 order book is a step-change (₹1,291 Crores versus ₹438 Crores) built on inflows of over ₹1,500 Crores in a single year, so the base for repeating that inflow is now much higher.

risks.risk: Raw material and cost escalation risk
risks.note: Fluctuations in the prices of steel, cement, fuel and other construction inputs may impact project costs and margins, particularly for fixed-price contracts. Mitigation relies on contractual price escalation clauses 'wherever feasible', strategic procurement planning and vendor diversification — leaving residual exposure on contracts without escalation protection, which matters at a 10.15% EBITDA margin.

EPC projects require significant working capital, and delays in customer certifications or collections can affect cash flows and liquidity. FY26 already shows the strain of scaling: trade receivables rose to ₹7,034.00 lakhs from ₹2,776.79 lakhs, the trade receivables turnover ratio fell 42%, the net capital turnover ratio fell 53% and the inventory turnover ratio fell 29% on inventory accumulated for newly awarded projects.

The construction industry remains labour-intensive; shortages of skilled manpower or disruptions in labour availability may affect project execution. GCC depends on a project workforce of 8,000+ personnel mobilised through an established network of site contractors, on top of its 1,400+ permanent employees.

Breakdowns or inadequate availability of construction equipment may delay project execution and reduce productivity. GCC's asset-backed model — 270+ owned machines and continuing IPO-funded equipment purchases — is both the mitigation and the source of the exposure, since utilisation of that fleet underpins the cost advantage it claims over third-party hire.

Construction activities involve inherent health, safety and environmental risks that may lead to accidents, project disruptions or regulatory liabilities. Client safety awards are a pre-qualification asset for GCC, so an incident carries commercial as well as regulatory consequences.

The Secretarial Auditor recorded that the Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, the Integrated Governance Filing under SEBI LODR and the Regulation 74(5) certificate were filed after the prescribed timelines, and that the delayed Statement of Investor Complaints for the same quarter drew a monetary fine from the Stock Exchange, since paid. Management attributes the lapses to the initial post-listing transition and says it has strengthened its internal compliance monitoring.
